meta.name: Global Health Ltd
meta.about: Global Health Limited operates a network of multi-specialty tertiary and quaternary care hospitals under the Medanta brand, primarily across North and East India. The company specialises in cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, digestive and hepatobiliary sciences, orthopaedics, organ transplantation, kidney and urology, and other complex medical procedures. As of June 2026, Medanta operated six hospitals across Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore and Noida, supported by an expanding diagnostics, pharmacy and outpatient network. [1]
meta.keyPoints: Hospital Count Global Health operates 6 hospitals across Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi, Lucknow, Patna and Noida, with 3,737 installed beds as of June 2026 across 5.6 million sq. ft. The network has 950+ ICU beds and offers services across 30+ medical specialties. Gurugram is the flagship hospital, while Lucknow, Patna and Noida form the newer hospital portfolio where capacity and clinical services are being scaled.[1]

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Global Health (Medanta), consolidated, ₹ crore. One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and an EBITDA margin on Screener's basis (after ESOP cost, before other income, post-Ind AS 116: lease rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest is in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is after leases). The bed build (Cluster 1, Cluster 2, other revenue) sits in `businessLines`; MEDANTA.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. Profit is attributable to owners (MEDANTA.patch.js). Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below (census beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB per cluster, plus pharmacy, labs and other operating revenue). FY27 +25%: Q1FY27 revenue +26.5% (IP volumes +28%, ARPOB +5.5%); Noida ramps from ₹91 cr of income in FY26 to ~₹420 cr; 418 brownfield beds (Indore cancer unit Q2/Q3FY27, Lucknow +172 in H2FY27, Patna +49 in Q4FY27, Noida to 550). FY28 +16%: brownfield beds fill, ARPOB +6%, Noida matures. FY29 +9%: an air pocket, because none of the five greenfields (2,950 beds) opens before FY30 on management's own timeline ('May of 2029... more FY30 numbers', 15-May-2026); growth comes only from occupancy and price. Street FY28E revenue ₹5,800-6,310 cr.

businessLines._why: Hospital revenue = census beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB (company definition: ARPOB excludes OPD pharmacy and other income; FY26 614,973 bed-days × ₹66,550 = ₹4,093 cr = AR in-patient ₹3,387 cr + out-patient ₹706 cr). Census beds per cluster are derived from disclosed bed-days and occupancy (Q1FY27: Cluster 1 93,663 ÷ (91 × 63%) ≈ 1,634; Cluster 2 79,401 ÷ (91 × 62%) ≈ 1,407; sum ≈ network 3,037). Cluster 1 (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi): beds 1,650 / 1,700 / 1,710 as the Indore cancer unit and Ranchi Unit 2 fill (Gurugram adds operating theatres and cath labs, not beds); occupancy 63% / 64% / 64.5% (FY25 64%, FY26 61% after Ranchi Unit 2, Q1FY27 63%); ARPOB ₹79,000 / 83,500 / 88,000 (+6.0%, +5.7%, +5.4%; FY26 ₹74,493, Q1FY27 ₹78,172; full-year ARPOB ran ~1.7% above Q1 in FY26). Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna, Noida): beds 1,520 / 1,720 / 1,760 (Noida 323 census beds at Jun-26 toward ~450; Lucknow +172 and Patna +49 installed beds); occupancy 62% / 64% / 66% (Lucknow + Patna 68%, Noida 30-40%); ARPOB ₹62,500 / 66,500 / 70,500 (Q1FY27 ₹61,742, +8.9%; Noida's NCR mix and possible tariff increases in Patna and Lucknow, where none has been taken). Other revenue (OPD pharmacy ₹183 cr, labs ₹44 cr, EPCG grants ₹56 cr, training, research and other ₹36 cr in FY26 = ₹318 cr): ₹360 / 420 / 480 cr with pharmacy +30% and labs +25% a year (Q1FY27 OPD pharmacy +51%) and grants falling to ₹30 / 25 / 22 cr. Greenfields (South Delhi, Pitampura, Mumbai, Guwahati, Varanasi) contribute nothing before FY30.

noida._why: GAM estimate inside Cluster 2: Q1FY27 income ₹85.5 cr, loss ₹4.9 cr; breakeven guided for H2FY27; PL expects ₹87 cr / ₹140 cr EBITDA in FY28-29E.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (after ESOP, before other income): 24.7% FY24, 24.0% FY25, 21.1% FY26 (Noida loss ₹78 cr; ₹56 cr of EPCG grants helped), 22.0% Q1FY27. Without Noida the margin rose from ~22.4% in Q1FY26 to 23.9% in Q1FY27. FY27E 22.4%: ex-Noida ~24.2% on ~₹5,090 cr plus Noida ~₹5 cr, less lower grant income. FY28E 23.2%: Noida ~₹60 cr EBITDA (~10% margin), Lucknow/Patna operating leverage, offset by doctors hired ahead of the new hospitals. FY29E 23.3%: growth slows to 9% and pre-opening costs for South Delhi and Guwahati rise. Company EBITDA (before ESOP, incl. other income) is ~2.5pp higher. Street FY28E (after ESOP, before other income): 24.2-25.9%. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹64 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~6% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Remaining project capex ₹4,858 cr over five years plus maintenance ₹600 cr over three years (Q1FY27 deck). Phasing (GAM): FY27E brownfield and Indore ~₹290 cr, maintenance ₹200 cr, South Delhi ~₹150 cr, Guwahati ~₹200 cr, Mumbai/Pitampura/other ~₹110 cr (Q1FY27 actual ₹161 cr; Mumbai and Pitampura still await approvals); FY28-29E ₹1,300-1,400 cr as Guwahati, South Delhi, Mumbai and Pitampura build out; includes ~₹30-50 cr a year of new leases (right-of-use additions were ₹216 cr in FY26). FY26 capex was ₹940 cr (₹416 cr Noida). The Varanasi built-to-suit lease will add a lease liability only on commencement (after FY29).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹223 cr (incl. ₹26 cr right-of-use) = 5.2% of average gross block (₹4,312 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use); Q1FY27 ₹69 cr (₹276 cr annualised). 5.0% gives FY27E ≈ ₹276 cr. Engine limit: capex is depreciated at once although greenfield spending sits in CWIP until FY30, so FY29E depreciation is ~₹40-50 cr too high (and we capitalise no interest).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities and debt, which is near zero (₹1,222 cr cash less ₹631 cr debt and ₹559 cr leases at Mar-26) and turns negative as capex rises. Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 28). (1) Treasury income = bank-deposit interest: ₹73.0 cr in FY26 on ~₹1,181 cr average company cash (Mar-25 ₹1,140 cr, Mar-26 ₹1,222 cr) = 6.2%; we apply 6.2% to average gross cash of ~₹1,220 / 1,120 / 1,000 cr (capex above operating cash flow draws cash down; part is funded with project debt): ₹76 / 69 / 62 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury items (rent ₹2.2 cr, miscellaneous ₹2.5 cr, interest on deposits at amortised cost ₹0.7 cr, a normal ~₹3 cr of liability write-backs): ₹8-9 cr. Left out as one-offs: interest on income-tax refunds ₹12.2 cr and the excess write-backs (₹7.8 cr in FY26). FY27E ₹84 cr vs FY26 ₹98.6 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, ex exceptional) ₹100 cr, of which ~₹20 cr were one-offs; Q1FY27 ₹22.2 cr (₹89 cr annualised).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits under other financial assets (non-current), not in Screener's cash: company cash ₹1,221.7 cr at Mar-26 less Screener cash ₹1,130 cr and investments ₹3 cr (Q4FY26 deck p.22; AR notes 11, 17-18).

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹79.1 cr in the AR (borrowings ₹30.0 cr, leases ₹44.6 cr, deferred payments ₹3.4 cr, other ₹1.1 cr; Screener shows ₹90 cr); Q1FY27 ₹26.7 cr (₹107 cr annualised) after the Noida loan's interest stopped being capitalised. New project debt is mostly capitalised during construction, so finance cost rises ~₹10 cr a year with new leases and debt on completed brownfield.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax less minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹213.3 cr, tax ₹56.0 cr (26.3%), profit to owners ₹159 cr = 25.5% leakage (DLF's share of GHL Hospital's loss adds back ~₹1-2 cr). FY26 effective 22.5% included prior-year credits; subsidiaries' losses get no tax credit.
assumptions._payoutWhy: First dividend ₹0.50 a share for FY26 (₹13.4 cr, ~2.4% of profit); capex absorbs cash.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt ₹631 cr and leases ₹559 cr are ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but a large metro build-out ahead.
dcf._tgWhy: Hospital demand grows with incomes, insurance and ageing; prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range, as for the other hospitals.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth stays ~9% a year to FY42E: the 2,950 greenfield beds (+80% capacity) open from FY30 and lift growth above 9% for some years, then maturity pulls it below; 9% is our average.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 25% (Screener basis) by FY42E: a little above FY24-25 (24-25%) as Tier-2 hospitals like Lucknow and Patna (~30% before ESOP) become a larger share, but held back because three of the five new hospitals (and Noida) are in costlier metro markets.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~20% of revenue (FY28-29E build) to 8%: replacement (depreciation ~6% of revenue) plus brownfield growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Noida reaches double-digit margins in FY28, Lucknow and Patna take tariff increases while volumes keep growing 20%, Gurugram adds procedures, and the greenfields stay on schedule.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Noida stalls near breakeven, Gurugram growth slows to mid-single digits, grants fade, doctor costs for the metro projects arrive early and the greenfields slip a year.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Medanta: EV/EBITDA on FY28E or Sep-28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 28x Sep-28E, Motilal Oswal 28x 12-month forward, Anand Rathi 28x and Choice 27x FY28E, Antique 27x FY28E, JM Financial 25x FY28E in Mar-2026). We use EBITDA after ESOP and before other income, post-Ind AS 116 (the model and Screener basis), with lease liabilities in net debt (consistent: rent is excluded from EBITDA and the lease debt is counted). 22.5x = Medanta's 25.8x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since listing (Nov-2022; no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 12.3% median de-rating of six listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Max, Fortis, Narayana, Rainbow, Jupiter; KIMS and Aster left out because new-hospital losses and the 2024 GCC demerger distort their history) = 22.6x, rounded to 22.5x. No growth premium: FY26-29E EBITDA growth (~21% a year) is mostly Noida swinging from loss to profit and is followed by an FY29 air pocket and five greenfields (three in Delhi and Mumbai) that earn nothing before FY30. Bull 30.5x and bear 21.5x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of its forward EV/EBITDA since listing.

Bull 54x and bear 38x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.

cover.headline: One of India's best hospital franchises, priced for a plan that starts paying only in FY30
cover.lead: Medanta runs six large super-specialty hospitals in North and East India (3,737 beds at Jun-2026), anchored by the 1,440-bed Medicity in Gurugram and by first-mover hospitals in Lucknow and Patna that fill at 68-70% and earn ~32% margins without price increases. Q1FY27 revenue rose 26.5% (in-patients +28%) and the new Noida hospital's loss shrank from ₹32 cr a quarter to ₹4.9 cr. Next comes a near-doubling of beds: 418 brownfield beds in FY27, then 2,950 beds in five greenfields (three in Delhi and Mumbai) that management expects to contribute "more FY30 numbers", for ₹4,858 cr of capex. The street values Medanta on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E or Sep-28E (25-28x)**. We forecast EBITDA (after ESOP, before other income) of ₹1,234 / 1,487 / 1,634 cr and EPS of ₹25.9 / 30.9 / 32.6 for FY27-29E. Applying **22.5x to Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,560 cr** (post-Ind AS, lease liabilities in net debt) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹1,271, DCF ₹572. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Gurugram is ranked India's best hospital (Newsweek 2026) and draws complex cases from across North India and abroad. Lucknow and Patna broke even in their first full year; in Q1FY27 they grew 28% at a 32% margin with no tariff increase in Patna in 4.5 years. In-patient volumes doubled from FY22 to FY26.

Noida swings from a ₹78 cr loss (FY26) to profit, 418 brownfield beds open and Lucknow/Patna keep compounding. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} and +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} and EBITDA in line with the street for FY27-28; our margin is lower (23.2% FY28E vs PL's 24.7%) because grant income fades and doctors are hired ahead of the new hospitals.

No greenfield opens before FY30, so revenue growth slows to ~{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} in FY29E while ₹1,300-1,400 cr a year of capex goes in; net debt (incl. leases) moves from ~zero to ~₹280 cr and ROE dips to ~15%. Our DCF (₹572) shows how much of today's price depends on the hospitals that open after FY30.

arguments.h: Valuation: at its own history while peers de-rated
arguments.p: At ₹1,365 the stock trades at 24.6x our FY28E EV/EBITDA, close to its 25.8x forward median since listing, while listed hospital peers had de-rated ~12% by 30-Sep-2026: that gives 22.5x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. The street (average post-Q1 target ₹1,630) pays 27-28x.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Noida breakeven (guided for H2FY27, now "earlier"), the Indore 80-bed cancer unit (end-Q2/early-Q3FY27) and Gurugram's extra operating theatres and cath labs.
Brownfield beds: Lucknow +172 (H2FY27), Patna +49 (Q4FY27), Noida to 550; any tariff increase in Patna or Lucknow.
Greenfield milestones: Mumbai (MHADA and environmental clearances), Pitampura building plans, South Delhi civil works, Guwahati construction.
Supply: block sales by Temasek (14.85%) or the co-founder (~10%), who sold 0.74% in May-Jun 2026.
Any O&M or acquisition deal ("a couple" under study, May-2026).

sections.title: Big, procedure-heavy super-specialty hospitals in North and East India, led by a famous founder

blocks.p: Medanta runs six large hospitals: the 1,440-bed Medicity in Gurugram (2009), Indore (175 beds), Ranchi (two units, 310 beds), Lucknow (778 of 950 planned), Patna (601 of 650) and Noida (433 of 550, opened Sep-2025), **3,737 installed beds** at Jun-2026, a quarter of them ICU beds. It is a tertiary and quaternary referral centre: heart (~21% of healthcare revenue), cancer (~14%), neurosciences, digestive and liver diseases (~11% each), kidney and urology (~8%), orthopaedics and transplants, with 100+ operating theatres and a heavy use of robotics. Gurugram, Indore and Ranchi make up **Cluster 1** (63% of FY26 income, growing ~10%); Lucknow, Patna and Noida make up **Cluster 2** (growing 37-55%). Around the hospitals sit 9 clinics, 12 labs, 22 pharmacies and 825+ collection centres.

Doctors are a mix of employees and full-time retainers working in specialty teams under department heads (2,480+ doctors). In FY26 in-patients brought ₹3,387 cr of revenue, out-patients ₹706 cr, pharmacy sales to out-patients ₹182 cr, labs ₹44 cr and government (EPCG) grants ₹56 cr. 56% of in-patient revenue was paid directly by patients, 25% by insurers on a cashless basis, 11% by CGHS, ECHS and the Railways, and international patients were 7% of revenue. There is almost no exposure to the low-priced government scheme PM-JAY.

sections.title: Demand is growing and insured, but everyone is building beds, especially in NCR

blocks.p: Indian private hospitals are in a capacity boom backed by demand that is still growing: health-insurance premiums rose 15.4% to ₹1.4 lakh crore in FY26 (40.8% of non-life premiums), GST on retail health cover was cut from 18% to nil in Sep-2025, 43.5 crore Ayushman cards had been issued by Mar-2026, and the Medanta AR cites private hospital revenue growth of 16-18% a year with ARPOB growth of 6-8%. Listed operators are expected to add ~15,000 beds. For Medanta the tailwind is real but uneven: Tier-2 cities in UP and Bihar (Lucknow, Patna) have little high-end supply, while Delhi NCR, where Gurugram and Noida sit and two of the five new projects go (Mumbai is a third), is the most contested hospital market in India.

sections.title: Revenue = beds × occupancy × ARPOB: Medanta has grown all three

blocks.p: Hospital revenue is the product of **census beds** (beds available for overnight patients), **occupancy** and **ARPOB** (average revenue per occupied bed-day; Medanta counts in-patient and out-patient revenue but not OPD pharmacy or other income). From FY22 to FY26 census beds rose 54% (1,779 → 2,737), occupancy stayed at 59-62% even as beds were added, and ARPOB rose 22% (₹54,547 → ₹66,550): hospital revenue grew ~2.1x. ARPOB has risen with case mix (more cancer, transplants and robotic surgery), price increases in Gurugram and CGHS, and shorter stays (ALOS 3.76 → 3.04 days; 2.87 in Q1FY27), which free beds for more patients. Unlike most listed peers Medanta's growth has been mostly volume: in-patients doubled from 102,000 to 202,000 a year.

sections.title: Two Medantas: a mature Gurugram-led cluster growing ~10%, and a Tier-2 cluster growing 30%+ at higher margins

blocks.p: **Cluster 1** (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi) earned ₹2,848 cr of income in FY26 (+9%) at a 24.4% margin (company basis), carrying all group overheads. Its occupied bed-days were flat in FY26 (the new 110-bed Ranchi unit diluted occupancy to 61%); ARPOB (+10%) did the work. In Q1FY27 it grew 10% with volumes +14% and margin 24.1%. **Cluster 2** (Lucknow, Patna and, since Sep-2025, Noida) earned ₹1,504 cr (+37%); without Noida, ₹1,413 cr (+29%) at a 31.5% margin. Lucknow and Patna run at 68-70% occupancy with lower ARPOB (₹61,742 in Q1FY27 incl. Noida, vs ₹78,172 in Cluster 1) but less legacy cost and no corporate overhead. Management says Lucknow and Patna still grow "in the upwards of 20%" on volume alone and that tariffs in Patna have not been raised in 4.5 years.

sections.title: Noida: from a ₹32 cr quarterly loss to almost breakeven in three quarters

blocks.p: Medanta Noida (550-bed capacity) opened in September 2025 and was formally inaugurated on 27-Nov-2025. Beds were opened floor by floor: 226 installed beds at Sep-2025, 328 at Dec-2025, 382 at Mar-2026 and 433 at Jun-2026 (323 census beds), with all 14 operating theatres, radiation oncology and robotics live from the start. The loss peaked at ₹32 cr in Q3FY26 and fell to ₹4.9 cr in Q1FY27 on ₹85.5 cr of income, after insurance, PSU and (in May-2026) CGHS empanelments. Management first guided breakeven in H2FY27 (15-May-2026), then said it would come "earlier than our previous expectations" (31-Jul-2026). Occupancy is still only 30-40%; hospitals of this kind break even at 40-45% (CEO).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Medanta has a real moat: the brand and clinical depth built around Dr Trehan and its department heads, recognised in global rankings, which pulls complex cases from across North India, the Northeast and abroad. In Lucknow and Patna the moat is close to a local monopoly on super-specialty care. In Delhi NCR and Mumbai, where half of the remaining capex goes, it is one strong brand among several (Max, Fortis, Apollo, Manipal), so returns there depend on execution rather than on scarcity. The moat also has a key-person element: the founder is still Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Cardiac Surgeon; management depth below him (Group CEO Pankaj Sahni, department heads) is real but a succession has not been tested.

sections.title: Revenue doubled in four years; the FY26 margin dip was Noida, not the core

blocks.p: Medanta's revenue grew from ₹2,167 cr in FY22 to ₹4,410 cr in FY26 (19% a year): +25% in FY23 as Lucknow and Patna filled, +21% in FY24, a slower +13% in FY25 (PL cites issues at the Lucknow unit; Noida was not yet open) and +19% in FY26. Profit attributable to shareholders rose from ₹196 cr to ₹556 cr (30% a year), helped by interest on the IPO cash. The EBITDA margin (after ESOP cost, before other income) climbed from 21% in FY22 to 24.7% in FY24, held at 24.0% in FY25 and fell to 21.1% in FY26, when the new Noida hospital lost ₹78 cr before it filled. Without Noida the margin kept rising (company basis 25.7% in FY26 vs 25.4%).

blocks.p: Medanta generated ₹624 cr of operating cash in FY25 and ₹714 cr in FY26, but spent ₹517 cr and ₹838 cr on hospitals and equipment plus ₹131 cr and ₹140 cr on land (Mumbai, Guwahati), so free cash flow turned negative in FY26 and debt rose ₹303 cr (Noida project loan). Returns have dropped as capital went in ahead of profits: Screener ROCE fell from 20% (FY24-25) to 17% (FY26); the company's own consolidated ROCE fell from 18.1% to 14.9% (21.3% excluding Noida and projects). sections.title: Earnings quality: clean books, but three EBITDA numbers, grant income and yearly one-offs

bullets: **Three EBITDA numbers.** Company EBITDA for FY26 is ₹1,056 cr (23.4% of total income): before the ₹38 cr ESOP cost and including ₹99 cr of other income. Screener (and our model) show ₹930 cr (21.1%) after ESOP and before other income; the AR P&L gives ₹919 cr on that basis (Screener puts ₹11 cr more into finance cost). Brokers use ₹919 cr. Always compare like with like.

**EPCG grant income in revenue.** Duty saved on imported equipment under the export-promotion scheme is booked as a government grant and released to revenue as export obligations are met: ₹55.8 cr in FY26 (₹16.2 cr in FY25), about 6% of EBITDA, boosted by the licences' transfer after the merger. ₹77.8 cr remains deferred. We assume ₹30 / 25 / 22 cr in FY27-29E.
**Doctors are partly outside employee cost.** Retainer doctors are paid "retainers and consultants fee" (₹658 cr, 14.9% of revenue) on top of ₹1,096 cr of employee cost; together ~40% of revenue.

**One-offs every year.** FY25: ₹49.9 cr stamp duty on the subsidiary merger. FY26: +₹19.6 cr EPCG interest reversal, +₹16.0 cr stamp duty reversal, −₹36.6 cr Labour Codes charge. Screener folds these into "other income" in its quarterly table, so its quarterly other income swings (−₹27 cr in Q4FY25, −₹15 cr in Q3FY26).

**Interest capitalisation.** Interest and costs of projects under construction are capitalised; when Noida opened its loan interest and depreciation hit the P&L (finance cost ₹26.7 cr in Q1FY27 vs ₹13.8 cr). The same will happen as each greenfield opens from FY30.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 77% of model-basis EBITDA in FY26 (70% in FY25; company: 68% of its EBITDA). Receivable days rose from 24 (FY24) to 34 (FY26) with CGHS and insurer dues; ₹15 cr of receivables were written off in FY26.

**Other income** was ₹99 cr in FY26 (14% of pre-tax profit): deposit interest ₹73 cr, interest on tax refunds ₹12 cr (one-off), write-backs ₹8 cr. We build it rather than extrapolate it (see Forecasts).
**Audit.** Walker Chandiok & Co LLP (Grant Thornton network), unmodified opinion. Leases are small (₹559 cr; lease payments ₹47 cr a year), so Ind AS 116 barely flatters EBITDA.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive accounting, and disclosure is good (cluster and Noida economics every quarter). We flag AMBER because reported EBITDA mixes in grant income that tripled in FY26, the headline company EBITDA includes other income and excludes ESOP, and a one-off line has appeared in each of the last two years. Read the margin on the after-ESOP, ex-other-income basis.

sections.title: Net cash of ₹591 cr before leases, about zero after them: a strong base for the build-out

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Medanta had ₹631 cr of bank debt (₹303 cr more than a year earlier, mainly the Noida project loan), ₹1,222 cr of cash and deposits (company figure, incl. ₹89 cr of longer deposits outside Screener's cash line) and ₹559 cr of lease liabilities (hospital buildings, land and equipment under Ind AS 116; ₹216 cr of new leases in FY26). So the company has **net cash of ₹591 cr ignoring leases**, or **net cash of ~₹30 cr including them**. Rent is small (lease payments ₹47 cr a year, ~1% of revenue), so the choice of basis matters less than at peers that lease most of their hospitals, but we keep it consistent: post-Ind AS EBITDA with lease liabilities counted as debt. CRISIL upgraded the bank loans to AA/Stable in Dec-2025.

sections.title: Ownership: founder at 33%, Temasek at ~15%, and Indian funds buying

blocks.p: Dr Naresh Trehan holds 33% (Jun-2026), with no pledge reported. The remaining financial investor is Temasek (Dunearn), in since 2015: it sold ~3 million shares (~1.1%) in Feb-2024 at ~₹1,315 (RJ Corp bought ~2.88 million) and held 14.86% at Mar-2025 and 14.85% at Mar-2026, i.e. no sale in FY26. What it means
rows: Complex specialist treatment (cardiac surgery, cancer, neurosurgery) and the most advanced procedures (transplants, robotic and experimental treatments), usually on referral.
Installed beds = all beds in the hospital, incl. day-care. Census beds = beds available for overnight patients; Medanta measures occupancy on census beds.

Average revenue per occupied bed-day. Medanta divides in-patient and out-patient hospital revenue (excluding OPD pharmacy and other income) by occupied bed-days.
Average revenue per in-patient: hospital revenue ÷ in-patient volume (disclosed from Q1FY27). It moves less with length of stay than ARPOB.
Average length of stay of admitted patients, in days. Shorter stays free beds for more patients and raise ARPOB.
In-patients (admitted); out-patients (consultations without admission, counted as encounters); OPD = out-patient department.
Medanta's hospital groups: Gurugram, Indore and Ranchi (formerly "mature") vs Lucknow, Patna and Noida (formerly "developing").

Operations and management contract: Medanta runs a hospital owned or co-built by another party (Ranchi Unit 2, Pitampura).

Third-party administrator: the insurer's agent for cashless hospital bills.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (Ayushman Bharat): the government's low-price insurance scheme for poorer families; Medanta has almost no exposure.
Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme: customs duty waived on imported equipment against future foreign-exchange earnings (international patients); booked as grant income when the obligation is met.
The accounting cost of employee share options; Medanta's own EBITDA excludes it, Screener's and ours include it.
Accounting rule that puts leased assets on the balance sheet: rent is replaced by depreciation and interest, and future rent appears as a lease liability.
DLF's 50% of GHL Hospital Ltd (the South Delhi hospital company Medanta controls); its share of profit or loss is not Medanta shareholders'.

Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the required annual return used to discount future cash (here the cost of equity, 11.3%; debt is small).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Global Health (Medanta), consolidated, ₹ crore. One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and an EBITDA margin on Screener's basis (after ESOP cost, before other income, post-Ind AS 116: lease rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest is in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is after leases). The bed build (Cluster 1, Cluster 2, other revenue) sits in `businessLines`; MEDANTA.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. Profit is attributable to owners (MEDANTA.patch.js). Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below (census beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB per cluster, plus pharmacy, labs and other operating revenue). FY27 +25%: Q1FY27 revenue +26.5% (IP volumes +28%, ARPOB +5.5%); Noida ramps from ₹91 cr of income in FY26 to ~₹420 cr; 418 brownfield beds (Indore cancer unit Q2/Q3FY27, Lucknow +172 in H2FY27, Patna +49 in Q4FY27, Noida to 550). FY28 +16%: brownfield beds fill, ARPOB +6%, Noida matures. FY29 +9%: an air pocket, because none of the five greenfields (2,950 beds) opens before FY30 on management's own timeline ('May of 2029... more FY30 numbers', 15-May-2026); growth comes only from occupancy and price. Street FY28E revenue ₹5,800-6,310 cr.

businessLines._why: Hospital revenue = census beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB (company definition: ARPOB excludes OPD pharmacy and other income; FY26 614,973 bed-days × ₹66,550 = ₹4,093 cr = AR in-patient ₹3,387 cr + out-patient ₹706 cr). Census beds per cluster are derived from disclosed bed-days and occupancy (Q1FY27: Cluster 1 93,663 ÷ (91 × 63%) ≈ 1,634; Cluster 2 79,401 ÷ (91 × 62%) ≈ 1,407; sum ≈ network 3,037). Cluster 1 (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi): beds 1,650 / 1,700 / 1,710 as the Indore cancer unit and Ranchi Unit 2 fill (Gurugram adds operating theatres and cath labs, not beds); occupancy 63% / 64% / 64.5% (FY25 64%, FY26 61% after Ranchi Unit 2, Q1FY27 63%); ARPOB ₹79,000 / 83,500 / 88,000 (+6.0%, +5.7%, +5.4%; FY26 ₹74,493, Q1FY27 ₹78,172; full-year ARPOB ran ~1.7% above Q1 in FY26). Cluster 2 (Lucknow, Patna, Noida): beds 1,520 / 1,720 / 1,760 (Noida 323 census beds at Jun-26 toward ~450; Lucknow +172 and Patna +49 installed beds); occupancy 62% / 64% / 66% (Lucknow + Patna 68%, Noida 30-40%); ARPOB ₹62,500 / 66,500 / 70,500 (Q1FY27 ₹61,742, +8.9%; Noida's NCR mix and possible tariff increases in Patna and Lucknow, where none has been taken). Other revenue (OPD pharmacy ₹183 cr, labs ₹44 cr, EPCG grants ₹56 cr, training, research and other ₹36 cr in FY26 = ₹318 cr): ₹360 / 420 / 480 cr with pharmacy +30% and labs +25% a year (Q1FY27 OPD pharmacy +51%) and grants falling to ₹30 / 25 / 22 cr. Greenfields (South Delhi, Pitampura, Mumbai, Guwahati, Varanasi) contribute nothing before FY30.

noida._why: GAM estimate inside Cluster 2: Q1FY27 income ₹85.5 cr, loss ₹4.9 cr; breakeven guided for H2FY27; PL expects ₹87 cr / ₹140 cr EBITDA in FY28-29E.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (after ESOP, before other income): 24.7% FY24, 24.0% FY25, 21.1% FY26 (Noida loss ₹78 cr; ₹56 cr of EPCG grants helped), 22.0% Q1FY27. Without Noida the margin rose from ~22.4% in Q1FY26 to 23.9% in Q1FY27. FY27E 22.4%: ex-Noida ~24.2% on ~₹5,090 cr plus Noida ~₹5 cr, less lower grant income. FY28E 23.2%: Noida ~₹60 cr EBITDA (~10% margin), Lucknow/Patna operating leverage, offset by doctors hired ahead of the new hospitals. FY29E 23.3%: growth slows to 9% and pre-opening costs for South Delhi and Guwahati rise. Company EBITDA (before ESOP, incl. other income) is ~2.5pp higher. Street FY28E (after ESOP, before other income): 24.2-25.9%. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹64 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~6% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Remaining project capex ₹4,858 cr over five years plus maintenance ₹600 cr over three years (Q1FY27 deck). Phasing (GAM): FY27E brownfield and Indore ~₹290 cr, maintenance ₹200 cr, South Delhi ~₹150 cr, Guwahati ~₹200 cr, Mumbai/Pitampura/other ~₹110 cr (Q1FY27 actual ₹161 cr; Mumbai and Pitampura still await approvals); FY28-29E ₹1,300-1,400 cr as Guwahati, South Delhi, Mumbai and Pitampura build out; includes ~₹30-50 cr a year of new leases (right-of-use additions were ₹216 cr in FY26). FY26 capex was ₹940 cr (₹416 cr Noida). The Varanasi built-to-suit lease will add a lease liability only on commencement (after FY29).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹223 cr (incl. ₹26 cr right-of-use) = 5.2% of average gross block (₹4,312 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use); Q1FY27 ₹69 cr (₹276 cr annualised). 5.0% gives FY27E ≈ ₹276 cr. Engine limit: capex is depreciated at once although greenfield spending sits in CWIP until FY30, so FY29E depreciation is ~₹40-50 cr too high (and we capitalise no interest).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities and debt, which is near zero (₹1,222 cr cash less ₹631 cr debt and ₹559 cr leases at Mar-26) and turns negative as capex rises. Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 28). (1) Treasury income = bank-deposit interest: ₹73.0 cr in FY26 on ~₹1,181 cr average company cash (Mar-25 ₹1,140 cr, Mar-26 ₹1,222 cr) = 6.2%; we apply 6.2% to average gross cash of ~₹1,220 / 1,120 / 1,000 cr (capex above operating cash flow draws cash down; part is funded with project debt): ₹76 / 69 / 62 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury items (rent ₹2.2 cr, miscellaneous ₹2.5 cr, interest on deposits at amortised cost ₹0.7 cr, a normal ~₹3 cr of liability write-backs): ₹8-9 cr. Left out as one-offs: interest on income-tax refunds ₹12.2 cr and the excess write-backs (₹7.8 cr in FY26). FY27E ₹84 cr vs FY26 ₹98.6 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, ex exceptional) ₹100 cr, of which ~₹20 cr were one-offs; Q1FY27 ₹22.2 cr (₹89 cr annualised).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits under other financial assets (non-current), not in Screener's cash: company cash ₹1,221.7 cr at Mar-26 less Screener cash ₹1,130 cr and investments ₹3 cr (Q4FY26 deck p.22; AR notes 11, 17-18).

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹79.1 cr in the AR (borrowings ₹30.0 cr, leases ₹44.6 cr, deferred payments ₹3.4 cr, other ₹1.1 cr; Screener shows ₹90 cr); Q1FY27 ₹26.7 cr (₹107 cr annualised) after the Noida loan's interest stopped being capitalised. New project debt is mostly capitalised during construction, so finance cost rises ~₹10 cr a year with new leases and debt on completed brownfield.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax less minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹213.3 cr, tax ₹56.0 cr (26.3%), profit to owners ₹159 cr = 25.5% leakage (DLF's share of GHL Hospital's loss adds back ~₹1-2 cr). FY26 effective 22.5% included prior-year credits; subsidiaries' losses get no tax credit.
assumptions._payoutWhy: First dividend ₹0.50 a share for FY26 (₹13.4 cr, ~2.4% of profit); capex absorbs cash.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt ₹631 cr and leases ₹559 cr are ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but a large metro build-out ahead.
dcf._tgWhy: Hospital demand grows with incomes, insurance and ageing; prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range, as for the other hospitals.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth stays ~9% a year to FY42E: the 2,950 greenfield beds (+80% capacity) open from FY30 and lift growth above 9% for some years, then maturity pulls it below; 9% is our average.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 25% (Screener basis) by FY42E: a little above FY24-25 (24-25%) as Tier-2 hospitals like Lucknow and Patna (~30% before ESOP) become a larger share, but held back because three of the five new hospitals (and Noida) are in costlier metro markets.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~20% of revenue (FY28-29E build) to 8%: replacement (depreciation ~6% of revenue) plus brownfield growth.
